title: R’ Yonah Butzrayah
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman describes him as R’ Mana’s student—Mana being R’ Yonah’s son. At the beginning of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim, chapter 9, he questions R’ Mana.
In Jerusalem Talmud Moed Katan 2:3, he asks R’ Huna whether he may sell books during the intermediate days of the festival.
He is also mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 2:7; Kilayim 8:3 and 8:4; Eruvin 3:1; Yoma, chapter 5, end of halakhah 1; Beitzah 2:8; Nedarim 9:1; and Nazir 6:9.

Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 5:1 and the supplied reference פר״ב, 11b, call him R’ Yonah ben Tzeruyah; 12a there has R’ Yonah ben Tzeriyah. In Pesikta Rabbati, Ki Tisa [HaShe’ar in the supplied Hebrew], at Hyman’s locator ס״ח, Hyman cites R’ Tanchuma son of R’ Yonah of Butzrayah. He is also mentioned in Midrash Shmuel, chapter 25.

notes.text: The references פר״ב, 11b/12a, and Pesikta Rabbati’s ס״ח remain unclear. The separate ben Tzeruyah, ben Tzeriyah and Butzraya forms are retained.

No whole primary scalar was returned for this entry. The Yoma 5:1 snippet is an inherited discovery lead, not fresh verification of Shabbat 5:1, the unresolved פר״ב11b/12a pagination or Pesikta ס״ח. Butzrayah, benTzeruyah and benTzeriyah remain distinct source forms, not one admitted identity. Hyman describes Yonah as Mana’s STUDENT; the parenthetical son of Yonah qualifies MANA, without making this headed Yonah his teacher’s father. שבעי is a questioning verb, not a person Shevai; רפ״ט is BEGINNING 9, not end. Yoma 5ENDhal 1 retains the end marker. All personal titles are abbreviated in the supplied source and remain R-prime, including both father and son occurrences; no blanket Rabbi title is supported. The unnamed MoedKatan/Gittin-style corpus continuation is contextual, not fresh edition proof.

The consulted Kilayim 9:1 has Yonah of Butzrayah putting a question to Mana. Moed Katan 2:3 names Yonah as the owner of the books asking Huna about selling them on the festival. The consulted Shabbat 5:1:4 names Yonah ben Tzeruyah in the discussion of Libyan converts. The parallel in Kilayim 8:3 has Butzrayah; the Arukh’s quotation under לבדקם has ben Tzeriyah. These spellings do not identify the edition behind פר״ב or establish a single person. At the end of Yoma 5:1 and in Midrash Shmuel 25:2, the consulted witnesses name Yonah of Butzrayah. Hyman’s print reads Ki Tisa, followed by ס״ח, where the supplied Hebrew reads HaShe’ar. The consulted Pesikta Rabbati 10, Ki Tisa, has Tanchuma bei Rabbi Yonah with the place form ממצוצרא. The older pagination remains unverified. For Nedarim, the specific name appears in the consulted 6:1:2, in the same discussion of cooked food as in Eruvin 3:1 and Nazir 6:9. Hyman gives 9:1.
